The rest stays on the SSD, and gets read as each token needs it.

scenes.headline: How a model bigger than memory runs off the SSD
scenes.sub: InferSSD's expert cache, read ring and read-ahead
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Hollis. Two engines did this the same week. Here is how the reads work.

scenes.title: The path of one missed expert

steps.say: A token of Qwen three point six uses eight of a layer's experts. InferSSD indexes each one's bytes inside the ordinary GGUF, and copies nothing.
Reads go through one ring, with direct I/O, so the page cache never keeps a second copy.
They land in a RAM cache whose size comes from the memory budget, and frequent experts stay.
And the CPU multiplies the expert right there. One token is one row, so moving it to a GPU buys little.
Done naively, the CPU waits for every read, and the drive waits for the router.
So every gate and up read goes first. Half of each expert's math starts while the down matrices still stream.
Cached experts need no read at all. But now the drive sits idle while the GPU runs the next layer.
So the next layer's router runs early on this layer's input, and the drive reads its likely picks into that gap.

parts.note: chance the next layer uses it
parts.say: Each speculative read is priced first. P is the chance the next layer really uses it.

parts.note: share still unread when the gap ends
parts.say: R is the share still unread when the gap closes. A weak guess on a long read gets skipped.

states.term: Hit rate: lookups served without a read
states.say: Local Code replayed real conversations on a DeepSeek model. With twenty-four gibibytes for experts, eighty-two lookups in a hundred never touch the drive.
At forty, ninety-four do. Routing is skewed, so a small cache holds most of what a conversation uses.

scenes.title: DeepSeek decode, tok/s, RTX 5090
scenes.say: On DeepSeek the README reports about seven tokens a second on an RTX five-oh-nine-oh, against under one for llama dot c p p. It publishes no number for either Qwen model.

steps.caption: 48 GiB of experts in memory, 17.0 tok/s
steps.say: Local Code does the same inside a Mac app. The post says thirty-two gigabytes. Its demo ran at a forty-eight gigabyte setting, on a sixty-four gigabyte Mac.

scenes.text: Streaming makes big MoE models run on small machines. The cache hit rate decides how fast.
scenes.say: Streaming makes the model run. The hit rate decides how fast, and neither post measured it.
